Build a surface from an orchestra manifest

Source: R/manifest-ingress.R
surf_from_manifest.Rd

Places effectsurf at the end of an orchestra chain: any member emitting an orchestra_manifest on a surfaceable inferential target can be rendered without first being refitted. The manifest's outputs supplies the grid.

Usage

surf_from_manifest(
  manifest,
  x,
  y,
  estimate = NULL,
  conf_low = NULL,
  conf_high = NULL,
  type = "prediction",
  labels = list(),
  transform = NULL
)

Arguments

manifest

An object exposing the orchestra manifest contract – inferential_target, outputs, and optionally summary and metadata.

x, y

Column names in outputs giving the two predictors.

estimate

Column name in outputs giving the response. Defaults to "estimate", falling back to "mean" when that is what the emitter used.

conf_low, conf_high

Optional interval column names.

type

Surface type, passed to new_effectsurf().

labels, transform

Passed to new_effectsurf().

Value

An effectsurf object.

Details

The function raises a typed refusal in six cases: the object does not present as a manifest; its inferential_target is not one a surface is meaningful for; the producer already abstained (summary$abstained); outputs is empty; no response column can be identified; or the named columns are missing or do not form a complete rectangle, which is the shape every downstream renderer assumes.

See also

effectsurf_refusal()
